title: Michelle Manes
text:
Michelle Manes




I’m a mathematician and Deputy Director of the American Institute of Mathematics (AIM). My research is in arithmetic dynamics and number theory, and much of my work centers on building and sustaining research communities — especially ones that widen who gets to do mathematics.
I’m also Co-Editor-in-Chief of La Matematica, the flagship journal of the Association for Women in Mathematics, and Associate Secretary for the Western Section of the American Mathematical Society.

title: Michelle Manes
text:
About
My research is in arithmetic dynamics — the study of number-theoretic and arithmetic-geometric questions that arise from iterating dominant self-maps of projective varieties — and more broadly in number theory and arithmetic geometry. I earned my Ph.D. at Brown University under Joseph H. Silverman.
For fifteen years I was on the mathematics faculty at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa, where I was Professor of Mathematics, and from 2018 to 2021 I served as a Program Director in the Division of Mathematical Sciences at the National Science Foundation. Since 2022 I have been Deputy Director of AIM, helping to lead one of the NSF-supported U.S. mathematical sciences research institutes.
Before returning to graduate school I spent a decade as a mathematics educator, and that experience continues to shape how I think about teaching, mentoring, outreach, and access to mathematics. I’m a Fellow of the American Mathematical Society (2024) and of the Association for Women in Mathematics (2020).

title: Research
text:
My research is in arithmetic dynamics — the study of number-theoretic and arithmetic-geometric questions that arise from iterating dominant self-maps of projective varieties — and more broadly in number theory and arithmetic geometry. Recurring themes in my work include moduli spaces of dynamical systems, post-critically finite maps, Galois theory of iterated preimages (arboreal representations), Belyi maps, and dynamical Mahler measure.
For the complete and current list, see Google Scholar, arXiv, or ORCID.

title: Teaching & Outreach
text: Before I became a research mathematician I spent a decade as a mathematics educator, and teaching, mentoring, and outreach have remained central to my work ever since — from doctoral advising to K–12 teacher professional development. I have taught mathematics at every level from third grade through graduate school; in public schools, private schools, charter schools, and summer programs; with special-needs students, girls, diverse urban populations, and Ivy League college students. In addition to all of this, I have extensive experience working with both preservice and inservice teachers.

title: Teaching & Outreach
text:
Outreach and broader impact
Since 2023 I have been a frequent presenter at Math Teachers’ Circles throughout Southern California and have worked with AIM staff on large public events, including the annual AIM Math Fair and the AIM Public Lecture Series.
Earlier, I founded the Math Teachers’ Circle of Hawai‘i (2011–2018), growing it from about a dozen teachers per session to sixty and sustaining it through a series of grants, and I developed a model for connecting remote circles on the outer islands to a hub in Honolulu. Other work has included co-organizing “Beautiful Day of Math” events on Moloka‘i and at UH Mānoa, teacher workshops across the Hawaiian Islands through the NSF-funded SUPER-M program, and guest sessions for teacher circles in Denver and Albuquerque.

title: Leadership & Service
text:
Deputy Director, American Institute of Mathematics (AIM) — 2022–present

I work closely with the Executive Director to create, manage, and oversee AIM’s scientific programs — more than 20 workshops and 60+ SQuaRE research groups each year — and I share responsibility for the institute’s leadership, budgeting, fundraising, and representation to the mathematical community. I was a major contributor to and co-PI on the $12.7M NSF award establishing AIM’s Research Conference Center (“A Model for Collaboration,” 2025–2030), and I oversaw AIM’s move to its new home on the Caltech campus.

Co-Editor-in-Chief, La Matematica — 2022–present

One of four founding editors-in-chief of the flagship journal of the Association for Women in Mathematics, published by Springer. We built the journal around equitable publishing practices — a doubly anonymous review process, a name-change policy, constructive reviews, quick turnaround, and an editorial board with exceptional diversity.

Associate Secretary, Western Section, American Mathematical Society — 2023–present

Responsible for the scientific program of two AMS sectional meetings each year and the Joint Mathematics Meetings every four years, and a member of the AMS Council. Associate Secretary in charge of JMM 2024 (San Francisco) and JMM 2028 (Philadelphia), and of the AMS Joint International Meeting in Armenia (2028).

title: Leadership & Service
text:
Previous roles

Program Director, Division of Mathematical Sciences, National Science Foundation — 2018–2021

Stewarded a portfolio of research and education awards — primary responsibility for 100+ proposals a year and shared responsibility for 500+ — across the Algebra and Number Theory, REU, CAREER, Focused Research Groups, Research Training Groups, and CDS&E programs. Helped propose a new “Research Initiation” program to support investigators launching their research careers.

Professor, Department of Mathematics, University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa — 2008–2023

Faculty member for fifteen years (Assistant, Associate, then full Professor), with an active research program and extensive departmental and university service. (See Teaching & Outreach for teaching and mentoring.)

title: Leadership & Service
text:
Building research communities

Roots of Unity workshop — co-founder and co-organizer, 2022–present

A workshop supporting graduate students’ transition to research in algebra, combinatorics, geometry, topology, and number theory, designed to build a welcoming and inclusive research community. Brought to the math institutes with funding I secured through a collaborative NSF grant.

Women in Numbers (WIN) — Steering Committee (Founding Chair, 2015–2019; member, 2019–present)

An international research network building collaborations and community among women in number theory. Co-organized WIN research collaboration workshops at the Banff International Research Station (2011, 2017) and edited the resulting proceedings volumes.


A complete list of grants and professional service is in my CV.
